vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.5

The skill bundle facilitates automated data collection from social media platforms (Douyin, TikTok, Xiaohongshu) via a local bridge and browser extension. It contains high-risk capabilities, specifically in `scripts/run.sh`, which supports remote command execution via SSH (`WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH`), and `scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh`, which can execute arbitrary shell commands provided via the `--bridge-cmd` flag. While these features are plausibly intended for remote deployment and bridge management, they provide a significant attack surface for remote code execution (RCE). Additionally, `SKILL.md` contains strict instructions to control the agent's response behavior, enforcing a synchronous 'closed-loop' mode that prevents intermediate user interaction.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (collecting data from a browser extension via a local bridge); it does not request unexplained secrets, but it can start arbitrary bridge commands and optionally SSH to a remote host, so you should vet any bridge startup command or remote host before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (browser-plugin collection via a local bridge) matches the included scripts and SKILL.md: scripts call a local bridge API (/api/collect, /api/status, /api/tasks/...), require curl/node, and include logic to start or wait for a bridge. Required binaries (curl, node) are appropriate for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts confine actions to the bridge API and local connector control (start, stop, status, task polling). The scripts enforce synchronous closed-loop execution as documented and print final JSON. They do not attempt to read arbitrary system files. Note: the scripts will attempt to auto-start a bridge using a user-supplied or auto-detected command and will SSH to a remote host if environment variables for remote mode are set (see below).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install/download step—this is an instruction-with-scripts skill. All code is included in the skill bundle; no network-based installer or remote archive is fetched by the install process itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which matches the code. However scripts honor optional environment variables (e.g., WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD, WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL). If those are set, the skill may execute the provided bridge command or SSH to a remote host — both of which rely on external credentials (SSH keys/agent) or may execute arbitrary commands. This is a legitimate feature for local/remote deployment but does require trust in any bridge command or remote host used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills or global agent config, and runs only when invoked. It will not autonomously run unless the agent invokes it (default behavior).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: control a local browser-connector to collect and export data. Before installing/using it, check these things: 1) Inspect any bridge startup command you pass (--bridge-cmd or WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD). The script runs that command via bash -lc (nohup), so a malicious or mistaken command could execute arbitrary code. 2) If you set WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH (or use remote mode), ensure the remote host is trusted and you understand what will run there; the script will SSH and execute the collector there. 3) Understand where exports go: export.tableUrl may be a cloud link or external service depending on the connector's exportMode; confirm the connector’s export destination and privacy. 4) Run the tool in a controlled environment first (no sensitive keys in environment) to verify behavior. If you do not intend to auto-start a connector or use remote execution, avoid passing --ensure-bridge/--bridge-cmd and do not set WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH.
